# Operations

Command syntax is generated from the installed live parser.
State mutations use the same `StateStore` as `ovcaq state`; requested
compare-and-set revisions fail closed.

## Commands

```text

ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state show
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state validate
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state get PATH
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state set [--unsafe] [--expected-revision N] PATH JSON
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state append [--unsafe] [--expected-revision N] PATH JSON
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state delete [--unsafe] [--expected-revision N] PATH
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task add [--expected-revision N] FILE
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task start [--expected-revision N] ID
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task attempt [--expected-revision N] ID FILE
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task complete [--expected-revision N] ID FILE
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task set-body [--expected-revision N] ID FILE
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task set-meta [--expected-revision N] ID FILE
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task set-status [--expected-revision N] ID {pending,in_progress,completed}
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state task clear [--expected-revision N]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state contract set [--expected-revision N] FILE
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] state restore [--expected-revision N]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow select [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow frontmatter [--available-tier KEY] --prd PATH [--expected-revision N] [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow phase-complete --outcome {converged,drained,more_prds,rework,tasks_done} [--expected-revision N] [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow resume-target [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow check-plan [--ceiling CEILING] [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow stall --prd NAME --site SITE --detail TEXT [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow park [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow defer --prd NAME --record FILE [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow complete-prd --prd NAME [--expected-revision N] [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] workflow render [--prd-root PATH] [--runtime-root PATH] [--state PATH] {audit,report,metrics}
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] status
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] doctor [--acknowledge-emergency]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] logs [--session ID] [--kind {raw,normalized}] [--follow] {purge} ...
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] logs purge (--session ID | --before RFC3339) [--apply]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] run [--no-tui] [--agent NAME]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] attach [--run-id ID]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] pause [--reason TEXT]
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] resume
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] stop
ovcaq [--root PATH] [--json] capability retry NAME
```

`stall` and `park` retain durable recovery intent and can be replayed after
every filesystem boundary. `defer` requires an `op_id` in its JSON record.
Audit and report renders publish deterministic Markdown; metrics renders to
stdout. Add `--json` before `workflow` for machine-readable results.

## Interactive operation

On an interactive terminal, `run` launches a supervisor and attaches the
TUI. Non-TTY `run` and `run --no-tui` supervise in the foreground.
Use `q` to detach while leaving the supervisor alive, `p` to pause at a boundary or
resume, `s` to stop the selected run after confirmation, and `?` to toggle
help. `attach` without selectors opens the fleet view; `--root PATH` selects
that project's detail view, and `attach --run-id ID` selects one live run.

Interactive `resume` attaches to the existing live supervisor, or launches
one when a boundary pause ended it. JSON runs require explicit `--no-tui`.
Noninteractive or JSON `resume` only clears pause; `attach` rejects JSON.
The selected theme is stored at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ovcaq/theme`, or `~/.config/ovcaq/theme` when unset.
An empty XDG_CONFIG_HOME uses the current directory. If the interactive view is
unavailable, OVCAQ reports the problem and falls back to plain output.

Workflow inputs use CLI flags, project `ovcaq.toml`, user
`${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/ovcaq/config.toml`, then package defaults.
`[workflow] prd_root` and `runtime_root` default to `docs/dev/project-management/prds` and
`docs/dev/project-management/ovcaq`; relative paths resolve from the discovered project root.
Runtime roots remain inside the project and reject symlink components.
`--prd-root` and `--runtime-root` override those inputs; `--state` overrides
the workflow state file independently of the runtime root.
Frontmatter receives the neutral tier keys `standard` and `deep` unioned with
the keys from `[agents.<agent>.tiers]` for the configured top-level `agent`.
An `[agents.<agent>.tiers]` table must now define `standard` and `deep`,
because the phase routes ask for those keys; a table that defines neither
neutral key silently falls through to the driver's own models instead of
failing. A PRD frontmatter floor applies only when its value is a tier key in
that table, so a floor whose value is a provider model name (`<model>`) warns
and applies no floor unless the table defines `<model>` as a key.
Codex reserves the tier value `default`, which keeps the Codex CLI on its own
configured model. Model values stay opaque. Repeated `--available-tier KEY`
flags supply the available keys explicitly; an unavailable hint warns and
applies no floor. This input reader does not launch or route agents.

Phase transitions require a running batch and an active PRD; only an empty
build-phase drain may omit the PRD. Batch finalization remains supervisor-owned.
Stall/park reject missing sources and conflicting destinations before committing
recovery intent. Source identity remains checked through intent publication.
An older unbound intent (step `intent`, artifact `null`) cannot move a PRD;
use `state restore` to recover its pre-intent backup. Bound recovery must
reconcile before restoration. Restoration does not move PRD files.

After a second consecutive park, the durable pause returns exit 4.
JSON output includes `ok: false`, `status: systemic_park`, and the committed
revision/result; human output asks the operator to inspect held PRDs and
the pause reason. Exact replay returns the same halt without another park.

## Workflow controller client

The external workflow controller is opt-in. Without `controller_argv`
there is no controller client, and nothing in OVCAQ invokes it yet: the
state store above remains the only workflow writer.

```toml
[workflow]
controller_argv = ["autopilot-controller"]  # argv array, never a shell string
contract_bundle = "contracts/controller-v1.json"  # pinned Contract A bundle
actor_file = "secrets/actor.json"  # credential path, needed only for apply
```

Relative paths resolve from the project root. The client checks the
controller's protocol major, bundle digests, advertised capabilities and
operations, and package version before any other call.

`python3 tools/autopilot-prerequisites --prd <ID> [--config PATH]` reports
whether a PRD's prerequisites are in place. It runs from the project root,
reads `./ovcaq.toml` unless `--config` is given, and never fetches or
writes. Exit 0 prints `{"ready": true, "prd": "<ID>"}`, exit 1 prints the
same object with `ready: false` and a `missing` list, and exit 2 means an
unknown PRD ID or a config error (stderr only). A predecessor counts only
as a regular `docs/dev/project-management/prds/done/000NN-*.md` file.
PRD 58 also needs `[workflow] controller_artifact` and
`controller_artifact_sha256`, with an `evidence` list holding `core`,
`jobs`, `reviews` and `records`, plus a `contract_bundle` and
`contract_bundle_sha256` precondition: a regular file reachable without a
symlink, whose bytes parse as a JSON object holding `protocol_major`,
`operations` and `capabilities`, and whose sha256 matches.
`contract_bundle_sha256` is the sha256 of the bundle file's raw bytes, the
digest `sha256sum <file>` prints, and the client checks the pinned bundle
against that same digest. PRD 61 also
needs `[autopilot] plugin_artifact` and `plugin_artifact_sha256`;
PRD 65 needs `[operator] client_artifact` and `client_artifact_sha256`. The
PRD 61 and 65 artifacts are each a JSON object of at most 16 MiB with no
symlinked path component, a matching sha256, and an `evidence` list holding
`AP00017` (61) or `Lantern00003` (65).

## Process identity and start preflight

`ovcaq doctor` reports six capability facts: `platform`, `advisory_lock`,
`process_group`, `group_signal`, `directory_fsync` and `process_identity`.
`process_identity` is `supported`, with the start token as detail, when the
libproc probe returns an identity, and `degraded` with the error text
otherwise. `ovcaq doctor --json` lists it under `capabilities` and reports
`ok: false` when it is degraded. OVCAQ reads process identity through
libproc and never spawns `ps`.

The start token is `"<sec>.<usec>"`, with microseconds zero-padded to six
digits. Tokens persisted in the former `ps lstart` form never match it, so
a supervisor still running across the upgrade reads as dead and its
records are cleaned up once; old tokens are not migrated.

A probe that cannot run is a `process_probe` error (exit 12): a non-darwin
platform, a libproc load failure, a returned size other than 0 or 136, or a
`pbi_pid` that differs from the requested pid. A zero-byte return always
means the pid is gone, regardless of errno. The message names the platform
and tells the operator to run `ovcaq doctor`.

Before any state write, `ovcaq run` validates the process identity probe
and the build, review and done phase routes; a failure leaves `state.json`
at the same revision. An unknown tier or a probe that returns no identity is
a `usage` error. A failure while publishing run metadata or the fleet entry
removes what was written, returns a fresh batch to idle or records an
attention notice on a resumed batch, and exits 1.
